info.title: auto-chatter external API
info.description:
The external API for servers that hold a workspace API key. A workspace admin issues the key in the dashboard. The key is shown once, and it reads only the data of its own workspace.

Every request counts toward a limit of 600 requests per minute per client IP address, before the key is read. Each valid key then has a limit of 60 requests per minute. Both limits apply to all paths together.

A contact write also counts toward the workspace's hourly write limit of its plan, which writes in the dashboard use too. A write refused with 400, 401, 403, 413 or 415 does not count toward it.

A flow start counts toward the same hourly write limit. A start refused with 400, 401, 403, 413 or 415 does not count toward it; every other start request counts, also a refused one and a repeated one.

The server does not serve this document.

get.summary: Describe the API key of the request
get.description: Returns the ID, name, scopes, workspace and expiry of the key in the Authorization header. Use it to check a key before a sync.

get.summary: List the comment contacts of the workspace
get.description:
Returns the comment contacts of the key's workspace in pages, in a fixed order of the connection ID and then the sender ID. Do not rely on this order: use only the cursor to read the next page. A contact is one comment sender on one connected Instagram account. Contacts of disconnected accounts are included.

To read all contacts, send the first request without `after`. Then send each next request with `after` set to the `next_cursor` of the previous page, unchanged, and with the same `connection_id`. Stop when `next_cursor` is `null`. Do not read or build a cursor: its format can change.

Each page is a separate read. A contact never comes twice in one full read, and a contact that existed for the whole read is never missed. A contact that is recorded during a full read at a position that the read has already passed is not in that read; it is in the next full read.

The response does not include the comment sender's username, consent state, comment or message text, or credentials. No field of a contact proves messaging consent or delivery eligibility.

The key needs the `contacts:read` scope.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of contacts in the page.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, unchanged.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: Only the contacts of this connected account. A cursor of another connection is refused.

400.description: An unknown or repeated query parameter, a `limit` outside 1-100, a malformed cursor or connection ID, or a cursor of another connection than `connection_id`.

403.description: The key does not have the `contacts:read` scope.

404.description: `connection_id` is not a connection of the key's workspace. A connection of another workspace gets the same response as an ID that does not exist.

patch.summary: Add or remove tags and set field values of one contact
patch.description:
Changes the tags and the field values of one existing comment contact of the key's workspace, and returns the contact after the change. A contact exists when the sender has commented on the connected account; this request does not create contacts.

Tags in `tags.remove` are removed first, then tags in `tags.add` are added. Tags that the request does not name stay as they are, also the tags that an agent added in the dashboard. Each tag is trimmed, normalized to NFC, lower-cased and normalized to NFC again, and has at most 40 characters. A contact has at most 20 tags.

A field is named by its ID from `GET /v1/fields`. The value must match the field type: a string of at most 1,000 characters for `text`, a number that a 64-bit floating-point value holds exactly for `number` (for example, `9007199254740993` is refused), a boolean for `boolean`, and a `YYYY-MM-DD` string for `date`. `null` clears the value. Fields that the request does not name stay as they are.

All changes of one request are applied together, or none is applied.

The request is idempotent: it sets a result state, so sending the same request again gives the same result. After a timeout or a `5xx` or `429` response, send the same request again. There is no `Idempotency-Key` header.

No tag or field value proves messaging consent or delivery eligibility, and this request sends no message.

The key needs the `contacts:write` scope.

requestBody.description: At most 16 KiB of JSON with the `Content-Type: application/json` header. At least one tag or field must be named.

200.description: The change is applied. The body is the contact after the change.

400.description: The request, its body or a path parameter is not valid. `invalid_request`: the request has a query string, the body is not JSON, names a key twice in one object, has an unknown key, names no change, has a tag that is not valid, names the same tag in `add` and `remove`, has more than 20 tags in one list or more than 20 fields, or a path parameter is not valid. `invalid_field_value`: a value does not match the type of its field, or a number has more precision than a 64-bit floating-point value holds.

403.description: The key does not have the `contacts:write` scope.

404.description: `connection_not_found`: the connection is not a connection of the key's workspace. `contact_not_found`: the sender has no comment on the connection. `field_not_found`: a field is archived or is not a field of the key's workspace. An ID of another workspace gets the same response as an ID that does not exist.

409.description: The contact would have more than 20 tags. Nothing is changed.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 KiB.

429.description: The client IP address or the key used its requests for this minute, or the workspace used its writes for this hour.

get.summary: List the contact fields of the workspace
get.description:
Returns the contact fields of the key's workspace that are not archived, ordered by name. Use a field's `id` to set its value with `PATCH /v1/contacts/{connection_id}/{sender_id}`.

The key needs the `contacts:read` scope.

400.description: The request has a query parameter.

403.description: The key does not have the `contacts:read` scope.

get.summary: List the flows that this key can start
get.description:
Returns at most 100 flows of the key's workspace that `POST /v1/flows/{flow_id}/starts` can start, in the order they were created: flows that are turned on, not archived, and whose published version starts with a direct message (a DM keyword or a DM default reply trigger). `connection_id` is the connected account of the flow's trigger; a start must name a contact of that connection. The flow definition and the message text are not returned.

The key needs the `flows:start` scope.

400.description: The request has a query parameter.

403.description: The key does not have the `flows:start` scope.

post.summary: Start a flow for one contact
post.description:
Starts one run of a flow from `GET /v1/flows` for one existing comment contact of the flow's connection, and queues the first message of the flow's published version as a direct message. The response does not promise that the message is sent: just before the send, the service checks again that sending is on, the run and the flow are still active, the 24-hour reply window is open, the person has not opted out and has explicit marketing consent, the contact and the conversation are not paused or handed off to an agent, and the plan's active contact limit allows the send. When one of these checks fails, the message is not sent and is not tried again later.

The message goes to the Instagram messaging account that the contact is verified to use: the account that received a private reply to one of the contact's comments and then sent a direct message. When there is more than one, the service uses the one with the most recent stored direct message among those that pass the consent and window checks.

The request is idempotent by `request_key`. Send a new UUID for each start, and send the same body with the same `request_key` again after a timeout or a `5xx` or `429` response. A request with a `request_key` that already started a flow returns that start with `202` and starts nothing new, also when the conditions changed since then. A `request_key` is never used again: a different body with the same key, or the key of a start whose data was deleted, is refused with `409 idempotency_conflict`. A refused request stores nothing, so a key refused with `4xx` can be sent again when the cause is fixed.

No contact, tag or field value proves messaging consent or delivery eligibility.

The key needs the `flows:start` scope.

requestBody.description: At most 4 KiB of JSON with the `Content-Type: application/json` header.

202.description: The start is accepted and the first message is queued, or the same request was accepted before. Sending is not promised.

400.description: `invalid_request`: the request has a query string, the body is not JSON, names a key twice in one object, misses a key or has an unknown key, or `flow_id`, `request_key` or `connection_id` is not a UUID, or `sender_id` is not a non-empty string.

403.description: The key does not have the `flows:start` scope.

404.description: `flow_not_found`: the workspace has no flow with this ID. `contact_not_found`: the sender has not commented on the connection. `not_found`: the path does not exist.

409.description: The start is refused and nothing is stored. The checks run in this order and the first that fails is returned. `idempotency_conflict`: the `request_key` was used for a different request or for a start whose data was deleted. `flow_unavailable`: the flow is off, archived, has no published version, does not start with a direct message, its published version sends no first message (for example a version that also changes tags or fields, or waits), or its trigger is on another connection. `sending_disabled`: sending is off for the service or for the connection, or the connection has no valid token. `no_dm_identity`: the contact has no verified messaging account. `recipient_opted_out`: the person revoked marketing or service messages. `marketing_consent_required`: the person has no explicit marketing consent. `reply_window_closed`: the person sent no direct message in the last 24 hours. `contact_paused`: automation is paused for the contact or the messaging account. `contact_busy`: the person has a conversation handed off to an agent, a flow run that waits for them, a pending follow-up, a recent direct message the service has not handled yet, or a first message of an earlier start that is not sent yet. `active_contact_limit`: the plan's monthly active contact limit stops the send.

413.description: The body is larger than 4 KiB.

415.description: The request does not have the `Content-Type: application/json` header.

429.description: `rate_limited`: the client IP address or the key used its requests for this minute, the workspace used its hourly write limit, the person was started in the last 10 minutes (by a direct message or by this API), or the connection started 700 flows in the last hour.

503.description: The service cannot answer now. `api_limit_unavailable`: the workspace write limiter is not available; the start is refused and nothing is stored. Try again later.

apiKey.description: `Authorization: Bearer ac_live_...`. The key is not accepted in the query string.

InvalidApiKey.description: The key is missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired. All of these get the same response. A key is revoked when the admin who made it is removed from the workspace or loses the admin role.

NotFound.description: The path does not exist. A path is checked only after the key is accepted.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path does not accept the method.

RateLimited.description: The client IP address or the key used its requests for this minute.

Unavailable.description: The service cannot answer now, for example when the request limiter or the database is not available. Try again later.

scopes.description: `contacts:read` reads contacts and fields. `contacts:write` also changes contacts. `flows:start` also lists and starts flows, which sends messages. A key with `contacts:write` or `flows:start` always has `contacts:read`.

next_cursor.description: The `after` value of the next page, or `null` on the last page.

Contact.description: The fields of the contact CSV export v1, with JSON names.

sender_id.description: The Instagram-scoped ID of the comment sender, as a string.

connection_username.description: The username of the connected account, not of the comment sender.

comment_count.description: The number of stored comments, as a decimal string.

automation_paused.description: True when automation is paused for the contact by hand or by a human handoff.

fields.description: The set values of the contact fields that are not archived, keyed by field ID. A number value is sent with all of its stored digits; read it with a parser that keeps that precision when it matters.
New values keyed by field ID. `null` clears a value.

value.description: A string for text and date (YYYY-MM-DD) fields, a number or a boolean.

connection_id.description: The connection of the flow's trigger. A start names a contact of this connection.

request_key.description: A new UUID for each start. Send the same key again only to repeat the same request.

connection_id.description: The `connection_id` of the contact. It must be the connection of the flow's trigger.

sender_id.description: The `sender_id` of the contact, as `GET /v1/contacts` returns it.

run_id.description: The flow run. It appears in the dashboard's flow run list.

status.description: Always `queued`: the first message waits for its final checks and the send.
